verdict.rationale: There is only indirect evidence for this story. Cal.com claims GDPR and CCPA compliance, which implies data-subject deletion rights. The MIT-licensed, self-hostable Cal.diy edition gives individuals and self-hosters full control over their scheduling infrastructure, and therefore over where data lives and how long it is kept. However, no documentation describes retention settings, deletion endpoints or account and booking purge controls. Missing for 10: documented retention policy or configurable retention windows, a documented deletion or erasure API or UI (including via MCP or agents), data export/deletion workflows, and independent corroboration.
